text:
The alt data on $META’s Muse is mixed heading into earnings.

Sensor Tower estimates 10.2M US downloads through Oct. 17, with daily active users up 15% week over week.

Early retention looks encouraging too. 23% of September installers were still coming back after two weeks. But search interest has cooled, and Meta is spending heavily to promote the app.

Meta’s $130–145B capex guide came before Muse launched. With ~$51B spent in the first half, I’m thinking $40–45B for Q3. If usage keeps growing, I wouldn’t be surprised to see them raise the annual guide or land near the high end.

Meta already expects a ~$10B Q3 legal charge, and today’s $25B New Mexico ruling adds more uncertainty.

The $10B charge alone is going to weigh heavily on reported earnings.

zh_summary: so $SPCX obviously blew the doors out with those earnings especially if Elon gets anywhere close to his goal of bringing 20GW online by next year. The question now seems to be what this means for every other neocloud. SpaceX is up today, the rest are flat to red. On one hand, $SPCX proved how important the neocloud business model is and how much demand is out there. On the other hand, $SPCX was so good that now people are doubting the ability for other neoclouds to easily finance their operations, how quickly those companies can bring compute online compared to Elon, and how much debt/dilution SpaceX themselves will have to take on to finance that buildout which then begs the question around how much dilution the smaller players will have to take on. SpaceX is also profitable whereas the others are years from profitability. My take is more that $SPCX has validated the entire concept of neoclouds which obviously have been under stress given the $CRWV bonds getting hit over the past two weeks, but the earnings were also so good that there might be more questions now about how well the others can execute. The broader theme seemed to be legitimized from those earnings: the compute constraints exist and have not eased up in any meaningful way.
